sentence: This project develops a systematic approach to combine genetic, tumor microenvironment, and computed tomography image signatures to distinguish aggressive from indolent early-stage lung cancer.
This project builds an AI method that tries to find how mutations in DNA change nearby genes and how DNA sequence controls gene expression.
This project builds computed tomography imaging methods with artificial intelligence to help diagnose inner ear disorders.
This project studies how cells in the cornea and their gene expression change after mustard exposure injures the eye.
This project engineers vascular cells that resist immune rejection and tests them in ischemic preclinical models.
This project uses genome engineering technologies to build maps of how genetic elements and sequence changes control genes and cells.
This project uses imaging to study how metastasis works in the lung at the single cell level.
This project tries to make optical coherence tomography systems easier to use for eye surgery.
This project studies which transcriptional, genomic, and clinical signs predict how well patients with Crohn's disease respond to therapy.
This project tests whether the diversity of consumed plant species is linked to gut bacteria across different human populations.
This project tries to understand how bone-building osteoporosis medications affect stem cells and osteocytes in bone.
This project develops ways to isolate and study the complexes of viral glycoproteins that herpes simplex viruses use to enter host cells.
This project provides single-cell genomics, spatial profiling, and computational modeling to study how lymphocytes interact and function in human tissues.
This project tests whether mRNA delivered in lipid nanoparticles can reprogram T cells to clear HIV reservoirs in lymphoid tissue.
This project develops an antibody drug that blocks Fas Ligand so tumor-specific T cells survive and kill tumors in patients with advanced cancer.
This project studies how choanoflagellates recognize and respond in immune defense, to learn about the ancestry of animal innate immune pathways.
This project provides bone imaging tools that measure tissue and cellular changes underlying musculoskeletal disorders.
This project uses mouse models to study why women are more vulnerable than men to Alzheimer's disease, looking at estrogen and astrocyte reactivity.
This project builds a sequencing method that finds somatic mutations in human tissue at the single-molecule level using a transposase.
